```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4
)
source("lab_submission.R")

lab_meta <- list(id = "lab01", title = "Introduction to R")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "What does lag(c(10,12,11,15,14)) return for the first element (in R with dplyr/stats lag)?",
  q2 = "Which package family provides autoplot() for tsibbles in this course?",
  q3 = "Does Australian Beer production look seasonal? Answer yes/no and one visual cue."
)
```

## What you will do

Open this file and click **Run Document**. Packages: `learnr`, `fpp3`.
Exercise chunks run when you click Run Code. They are not knitted in one pass.

## Setup
```{r setup-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=4}
library(tidyverse)
library(fpp3)
```

## Vectors and tibbles
```{r vec-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=12}
sales <- c(10, 12, 11, 15, 14)
mean(sales)
lag(sales)
df <- tibble(time = 1:5, sales = sales)
df |> mutate(lag1 = lag(sales)) |> filter(sales >= 12)
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("NA", correct = TRUE),
  answer("10"),
  answer("14"),
  answer("0"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## First time plot
```{r plot-ex, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
aus_production |>
  autoplot(Beer) +
  labs(title = "Australian beer production", y = "Megalitres")
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("fpp3 / feasts / ggplot2 for tsibbles", correct = TRUE),
  answer("base graphics only"),
  answer("Excel pivot tables"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "e.g. Yes — repeating quarterly peaks …",
  trim = TRUE
)
```

## Submit

Answer the questions above first, type your name, download the `.txt`, and upload it.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
